Title: Got me ..........Yep, got me good!!
Review:
Smartphones are to the point where it becomes necessary for the consumer to understand precisely what their needs are, how responsible they are in managing expensive technology, and exactly what value do they place on their personal and private data.
Having said this approximately 95% of users/consumers utilize perhaps +/- >5% of the technology in todays smartphones (this infers flip phones are more appropriate and less crowded bandwidth is a good thing). 
I tend to "upgrade" every other year or even skip two years based upon advanced technology from what I may currently "use". What I consider "use" is a tool, nothing more, nothing less. Every facet of the tool is used as to what the intended purpose of its installation on the device. Upon completing a task with this tool, it's simply put away until it's required to assist in another function. Nothing more.
In other words, it's a work place assistant not a pacifier, not an addition to my hand, nor my ear nor a cause of a 3 car pileup on the 5.
This brings me to the Samsung S26Ultra which caught my attention forcing me to a degree to trade in the very trusty but lacking features, S24Ultra. Mind you the 24 was a brilliant introduction to a grip on perhaps a new direction if implemented responsibly, that being Ai (Advanced Intelligence, nothing about it is artificial) the upgraded to the S26 Ultra Advance Intelligence that was the game changer for me was, "generative Ai" 
This feature was lacking in previous models. For me as a photographer, I sometimes am unable to have the full setup available at the ready and yet I need to capture a moment real time. The "fluff" around the capture on the S24 can be removed but substituted by what ever was whatever. Generative Ai allows me to place any and every background (within reason) so as to present a moment easily described to a client.
The Snapdragon processor has GPU power second to none and frankly blows past many laptops. The screen is a privacy screen, which I've gotten used to, and become extremely pleased with. The BBY trade-in during the launch period gave a double storage deal I could not refuse and seriously, provided a best of breed value, albeit "smart phones are getting too pricey" unless you know how and what you're intended usage is and how responsible the user is implementing this tool.
Again, my primary use for this tool is the quick use of the camera, and BTW the Pro setting both still and video are an amazing feature setup. Rather than mess with setting up every time, I've pre-set 3 settings I normally use, day time, night time and some secret and have them locked and loaded in presets in a folder next to my camera app and easy to go.

Title: The Upgrade I Actually Felt (S23U to S26U)
Review:

The "Privacy Display" is Magic: This is the sleeper feature of the year. It’s built into the panel (Flex Magic Pixel tech), so I don't need those ugly plastic screen protectors. I can tilt my phone on the plane or in a meeting, and the screen just "blanks out" for everyone but me. It’s a game-changer for working in public.

Performance & Thermal Efficiency: The Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 is a beast. My S23U used to get warm during long 4K recording sessions or heavy gaming. The S26U stays significantly cooler, and the 16GB of RAM makes the new One UI 8.5 feel instant.

Charging Speed: Finally, we’re at 60W. Moving from the S23’s 45W doesn’t sound like much on paper, but I’m hitting 75% in about 30 minutes. When you’re in a rush, those extra 15W matter.

The Camera Polishing: While we lost the 10x physical optical from the S23U, the new 50MP 5x sensor paired with the Gen 5 NPU actually produces cleaner shots at 10x-20x than my old dedicated lens did. The "Horizon Lock" on video is also incredibly smooth—perfect for capturing kids or pets on the move.

Bottom Line: The S23 Ultra was a legend, but its time is up. The S26 Ultra feels like a professional tool again, rather than just a "smarter" phone. Best Buy’s trade-in process was seamless, and for the price of a mid-range watch, I’ve reset my 7-year update cycle.

Title: Product is great - Delivery was not
Review: I'm loving my new phone. Camera, customizations, speed, and graphics are great in my opinion. Delivery was a real hassle. Which is why I gave 4 stars. I show up on 3/13 and was told by store personnel that there is a process in which to go through and that usually take at least 5 business days. I was informed that their CS was actually located in a completely different country and they truly don't know what goes on in each individual store. I left the store and immediately called CS again and vented my frustrations. I was told that my issue would be prioritized and I would receive and email within 24 hours. Roughly 48 hours later, I get the email and send the requested information and within a few mins of sending that email, they released the replacement phone. Had CS been up front about their process, a lot of my frustrations wouldn't have even happened. There needs to be better communication from CS to the customer. Best Buy did make everything right and I received my replacement as promised. I want to thank the store personnel at the Lexington, SC location for being up front and explaining everything and taking the time to help me through this whole process. FYI, don't ship electronics to your home if there's an option for pick up in the store. Apparently, delivery drivers like to cut a little slit in the corners and take the product before it reaches you. Ship to store and pick up there is best. My lesson was certainly learned and will follow this going forward!!

Title: Not really an improvement over my S23 ultra
Review: The S26 ultra touts a couple of new features, notably 25 watt wireless charging and a privacy display screen. The fast charging requires that you have a case with a magnet, it doesn't work with the bare phone. It doesn't work with most cases, either, because they're too thick or don't align precisely. I have a Zagg "Crystal Palace" case, and I haven't seen anything faster than 12 watts. The privacy display works, but the screen appearance degrades significantly with it on, and the screen's still quite readable at up to about 45 degrees. If you're buying the S26 ultra for this feature, you'll probably be disappointed. The S26U has a faster processor, but that only really matters if you play graphic-intensive games on your phone. I play games, but only really on my PC or tablet, and many phone games aren't that demanding. The S26U is still a good phone, just probably not worth the upgrade if you own a high-end phone that's only a few years old. Title: trade in option by best buy is a scam
Review:
I had one of the worst customer service experiences I’ve ever had with Best Buy’s trade-in program, and I would strongly advise others to be very careful.

I traded in a Samsung Galaxy S22 Ultra that had no cracks and was in good condition. Before shipping it, I even had the device inspected in-store at their Oswego Route 34 location, where a Best Buy employee confirmed it was in good condition.

After they received the device, I was shocked to be told that the phone was “shattered on the screen and back,” which is completely inaccurate and does not reflect the condition it was in when I shipped it. When I asked for photo evidence of this supposed damage, I was told that they do not provide any pictures—so there is no transparency or way for customers to verify their claims.

To make matters worse, I was then informed that because they classified the phone as “cracked,” I would lose the promotional trade-in value entirely. This means customers are expected to accept their judgment without proof, even when it contradicts prior in-store verification.

Their terms and conditions place all responsibility on the customer for any damage during shipping, even though they provide the shipping label. This creates a system where the customer carries all the risk with no accountability from Best Buy.

In the end, I chose to have my phone returned rather than accept a drastically reduced value with no evidence provided. I will also be returning the new phone I purchased and taking my business elsewhere.

This experience showed a complete lack of transparency, accountability, and fairness. I expected much better from a company like Best Buy.
